LESSON: WESTERN STYLE SOLO SONGS

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: MUSIC AND DANCE FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Performing
Topic 2.2: Western Style Solo Songs
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 11

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Western Style Solo Songs, part of Performing in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 MUSIC AND DANCE FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: How does one prepare to perform a Western solo song? 2. Why are performance techniques important in Western solo songs?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Western Style Solo Songs together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Self-efficacy: The learner confidently performs arias and western solo songs before an audience using the

techniques learnt.

● Citizenship: The learner performs western solo songs gaining knowledge on other global cultures.

● Learning to learn: The learner identifies challenges in executing performance styles in western solo songs and

seeks clarification of how to perform them.

Digital literacy: The learner utilises digital devices with appropriate assistive technology to source for and

record performances of Western solo songs.

Values:
● Respect: The learner appreciates others’ views when giving and receiving feedback on their performances.

● Integrity: The learner acknowledges the source of pieces of music sourced from online platforms and from

other musicians for performance.

● Responsibility: The learner uses digital devices with appropriate assistive technology for the intended

purposes.

● Social justice: The learner gives objective views on peers’ performances.

● Peace: The learner works in harmony with others as they rehearse, perform and critique others’ performances.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Healthy Relationships: The learner collaborates with others in group work as they discuss, rehearse, perform

and critique their performances.

● Life skills: The learner grows their music talent by learning styles and techniques of rehearsal and

performance.

● Cyber Security: The learner uses digital apps responsibly as they source and record music.

Suggested Learning Resources

Song book in appropriate print and braille format, ICT devices with appropriate assistive technology, Internet

connectivity, Exercise books in appropriate print, Sheet music in print and in braille, Resource persons,

Suggested Key Skills Assessed

• Describing the performance style of selected Western solo songs.

• Performing a Western style solo song using appropriate performance techniques.

• Performing a Western style solo song observing prescribed performance directions.
